focus.why: Biopsy negative for neoplasm/infection; imaging shows osteolytic C3-7 lesions with cord compression; supports non-neoplastic bone lesion.

payload.query: Need complete cervical spine MRI/CT with contrast, biopsy histopathology and immunohistochemistry report, serum calcium, phosphate, PTH, alkaline phosphatase, renal function, SPEP/free light chains, and mycobacterial/fungal cultures (core to distinguish non-neoplastic metabolic/inflammatory bone lesion from occult neoplasm/infection).
payload.retrieval_output: The resected specimen exhibited various and complex proliferating patterns of vasoforming cells in low-magnification images, with most areas showing a combination of solid and vasodilated proliferating patterns. In solid areas, numerous vascular cavities had been formed by atypical cells, including epithelioid cells with infrequent mitosis. In the periphery, irregular nodules had infiltrated into the adjacent muscular and fatty-fibrous tissue. The nodules had a slit-like structure with spindle cells. Several nodules contained epithelioid cell proliferation that clearly showed ERG, CD31, and CD34, but not D2–40, immunopositivity, which were surrounded by cells positive for the pericytic markers myo1B, CD146, and SMA. The proliferating cells were negative for markers of epithelioid hemangioendothelioma, including CAMTA1, TFE3, and FOSB. The Ki-67 labelling index was calculated as approximately 16.1% (109/678) in areas with solid components and dilated capillaries and 10.6% (83/783) in areas containing slit-like blood vessels in the solid components.

payload.analysis: Consensus favors cervical spine vascular neoplasm, likely angiosarcoma: atypical vasoforming cells, ERG/CD31/CD34+, myo1B/CD146/SMA+ pericytes, Ki-67 10.6-16.1%, muscle/fat infiltration. Negative EHE markers and cultures exclude EHE, infection, non-neoplastic lesion. MYC/TP53, resection details, molecular panel, HIV/HHV-8, MRI/MRA missing. All available key evidence covered; angiosarcoma leading.

payload.report: An 80-year-old woman had progressive right upper limb weakness, gait disorder, neck pain and sensory loss with an osteolytic C3-7 mass compressing the cervical cord. Biopsy showed atypical vasoforming cells positive for ERG/CD31/CD34 and myo1B/CD146/SMA, Ki-67 10.6-16.1%, infiltrating muscle and fat; cultures and inflammatory/tumor markers were negative, refuting infection and non-neoplastic causes. Negative D2-40/CAMTA1/TFE3 excluded hemangioendothelioma and hemangioblastoma, leaving cervical spine angiosarcoma as the leading diagnosis.
